questions.question: What is the key difference between display: none and visibility: hidden?
options: display: none deletes the HTML tag permanently
display: none completely removes the element from the layout taking 0px space, while visibility: hidden leaves an empty space
visibility: hidden only works on text
questions.hint: One takes up layout space, the other does not.
questions.explanation: display: none collapses the element out of the layout entirely, whereas visibility: hidden hides it while preserving its geometric footprint.

questions.question: An element with position: absolute positions itself relative to which ancestor?
options: The nearest ancestor with a position other than static
questions.hint: Nearest positioned ancestor (relative, absolute, fixed, sticky).
questions.explanation: An absolute element positions relative to its nearest ancestor whose position is not static; if none exists, it defaults to the viewport.

questions.question: Which position value keeps a navigation bar pinned to the exact same screen location while the user scrolls?
questions.explanation: position: fixed locks an element relative to the browser viewport, keeping it visible regardless of scrolling.

questions.question: How does position: sticky behave during scrolling?
options: It is permanently fixed at all times
It behaves as normal flow until a scroll threshold is met, then pins within its parent container
It hides the element on scroll down
questions.explanation: position: sticky toggles between relative and fixed positioning depending on the user's scroll position within its parent container.

questions.question: What is the default position value for all standard HTML elements in normal flow?
questions.explanation: position: static is the default positioning for elements in the document flow.
